records.words: Back to the valley. Last time I left bored on 18 July with Zehra delaying. This edition says a spoken answer during visits. I want to check the ledger and the rain date first.
It starts at the beginning again, at seven in the morning. I know the margin is tight, so I will call for the barley first, as before.
Before waiting, I want to see what else I can order. Last time I only knew call, visit and send grain.
Writing to the landowner is new to me and it states when I may use it. Good: a constrained recovery if the grain falls short. Both are disabled for now, with reasons.
Zehra delays again for her own barley, same as last time. This edition promises a spoken answer during visits, so I will go to her rather than insist.
Her question about feeding her family is fair. I will visit, and this time not send grain until I know the sack size. I remember it was six measures.

The same start as last time: call made, five came, Zehra delays for her own barley. I am walking to her house. But the clock has said 08:00 for twenty-five seconds and still 20 minutes until arrival. Perhaps reading this house page holds the day. I will go back to the notebook to let it move.
Back at the notebook the day jumped to 08:30 and I am at her house now. Seven delayed this time, two more than I expected. I want to see the spoken answer while I am sitting with Zehra.
There it is, a spoken line: I came to listen. That is what I wanted last time instead of insisting.
My words are shown plainly. No answer from her yet. I learned the house page holds the clock, so I will return to the notebook and wait for her reply.

The picture is clear: lines from the residence to every house, a red pin at Çoban, a rain bar at the top. But the clock has sat at 08:30 for half a minute. Seven unanswered delays seem to hold the whole valley still. I am waiting, but for what?
An hour passed in thirty seconds. Yusuf said Come in, not much more than last time. Did Zehra answer my I came to listen? Checking her house before I leave.
My I came to listen has vanished from the page. Only Come in. I cannot tell whether Zehra heard it or what it changed. Opening About to see their food situation before deciding on grain.
Same family, almost no food, a birth coming. This time I know the sack is six measures and that it leaves no margin. I am choosing it knowingly. Yusuf thanked me last time.
Better than last time: it says plainly Sent grain to the Çoban house. Still no amount. I will check the ledger figures.

Twenty-four in the granary, five cut, about 350 standing: 379 against 384 owed. I am already five short if nothing else is found. It is only an estimate, but I gave the grain knowing it was tight. The writing-to-the-landowner order may matter later.

I am following the same path as last time and it plays the same: one visit, one sack, Come in. The spoken line was welcome, but I saw no answer to it. Half an hour of game time per thirty seconds, and now nine people delaying. I am walking home.
Last time Information said replies slow time. I want to know if there is a way to acknowledge the delays without insisting.

Still only insist for a delay; no way to accept one. I notice Reduce a household payment is possible, which I had not seen. Rain is two days off and only ten measures are cut. I will let the day run and see whether the delayers come once their own barley is in.

Yusuf’s thanks this time is drier: thank the landowner, or God instead. Not the warm I won’t forget who sent this. I am home. Three from Tepe are delaying; I will try visiting them and saying I came to listen.
Again the clock sat at 10:30 for twenty-five seconds. It seems to move in half-hour jumps. I cannot tell when the day is actually moving.
Zehra is gone from the delayed list and Çoban has an empty circle; fifteen came. I think she came after her own barley, without my insisting. That pleases me. I am at Tepe now.
Said it again. The household is only Someone from the Tepe house; no names. Looking at About.
Requested phone check starting. Tepe jars look low by my guess. I will not send more grain; I am already short.

Requested phone check: Back to the notebook worked. On the phone the map is small, my location line is cut off at at the Tepe house. 50 game minutes left h..., the house row is cut at both edges, and only one delayed reply fits above Skip. Readable but cramped. Back to the laptop.

This is the same afternoon that lost me last time. Two visits, two Sit down or Come in, my I came to listen with no visible answer, and eight identical delays. Half an hour of game time takes thirty real seconds. I would leave here, but I have set the time aside, so I will try Skip, which I never used before.
Trying Skip to reach the next event. It says it keeps the slowdown, so I hope I will not miss a reply.
Skip greyed out and the clock only moved half an hour, the same as waiting. Two Tepe people came after my visit; seventeen now. I will check how much is cut.

Thirty-five cut now, and the total reads 389 against 384, five over where it was five under. The estimates move and I cannot tell why. Further than last time, but it is still one long afternoon. I want to see the twentieth.
Home at one o’clock. Visiting seemed to bring the Tepe people and Zehra, or at least they came afterwards. I will try the same at Demirci; it is the only thing I can do besides insist.
Third time the same single line. I would like to hear what they actually say back. Saying it once more.
Steward, sit down if you’re staying. A little more character than Sit down, but still nothing that answers what I said. I am waiting through the visit.

Twenty came, but the Demirci delays did not change after my visit. Three visits now, each a one-line welcome and my one line back. Nine real minutes and it is still the eighteenth at three o’clock. The only lever I have left is insisting, and I do not want to.
Looking at earlier replies to see whether any of my words were answered somewhere I missed.

This record is what I like: You had 6 grain measures carried, and You have not asked for work or promised grain after each of my words. Plain and countable. Zehra is named among those who came. But nobody answered my listening; the record only notes that I said it.
Home again. I have nothing new to do, so Skip once more to see whether it reaches evening or the next day.
Skip greyed itself again and the half hour passed at the same speed as before. I do not understand what Skip skipped. Visiting Kuyucu, since visits are the only thing that seems to move people.
At Kuyucu. Before saying my one line, I will read who they are.
A well-digger and two daughters, low jars. Everyone has low jars and barley at home. The houses are starting to blur together. Saying my line again.
We weren’t expecting you. I like that one; it is honest. Twenty-two came. Still the eighteenth at five o’clock after eleven real minutes.

Four visits, four one-line welcomes, my one line each time. The welcomes have a little character, but I am going round the houses to pass the afternoon. Twelve minutes in and the rain is still two days away.
Six o’clock, walking home. Checking the harvest before evening.
A hundred cut, 260 standing; 384 total, exactly the debt again. A third of the field cut in one day is real progress, and I can see it. Waiting toward evening.
Seven in the evening, nothing new. I am only watching the clock now.
Eight in the evening, still the eighteenth, and nothing has changed for two minutes. I have reached my set time. I will look at Feedback and stop.

I am stopping at eight in the evening on 18 July after fifteen minutes. This time I knew the sack size, the record wrote every gift and word plainly, and a third of the barley is cut. But I spent the afternoon walking house to house saying the same single line and hearing a one-line welcome, with no answer to what I said and nothing to decide except whether to insist. It is the same long first day that lost me last time, only further along. I selected I am stopping in Feedback; the game put those words in the note itself. I typed nothing and submitted nothing. I would return another evening to see whether the barley is in before the rain, if my place is kept and the days move faster once I have nothing to answer. I would not leave it running.
